Compute the Jacobian of the residual map G

Source: R/sim.R
sim_residual_jacobian.Rd

The function computes the Jacobian matrix of the residual map with respect to the attractivenesses. The function returns NA when applied to spatial interaction models for which the map is not defined.

Usage

sim_residual_jacobian(sim, ...)

Arguments

sim

a spatial interaction model, an object of class sim

...

additional parameters

Value

a \(p\times p\) matrix, where \(p\) is the number of destination locations, or NA when the residual map is not defined

Details

The residual map \(\mathbf{G}\) is given by

$$G_j=D_j-\kappa_j Z_j,$$

where \(D_j\) is the destination flow (destination_flow()), \(Z_j\) the attractiveness (attractiveness()) and \(\kappa_j\) the conversion factor (sim_conversion()), all attached to destination \(j\). The equilibria of the Harris and Wilson model (see blvim()) are the zeros of \(\mathbf{G}\).

The derivatives of \(\mathbf{G}\) w.r.t. \(\mathbf{Z}\) can be used to analyse the stability of the solutions, among other applications.

See also

sim_potential(), sim_conversion(), destination_flow()

Examples

distances <- french_cities_distances[1:10, 1:10] / 1000 ## convert to km
production <- log(french_cities$population[1:10])
attractiveness <- log(french_cities$area[1:10])
model <- static_blvim(distances, production, 1.5, 1 / 250, attractiveness)
sim_residual_jacobian(model) ## must be NA
#> [1] NA
dyn_model <- blvim(distances, production, 1.5, 1 / 250, attractiveness)
sim_residual_jacobian(dyn_model)
